title: Elevation Certificate and Coastal High-Hazard Zone Requirements, Excess Flood Tiers
content:
**Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** tiers differ in whether a home in coastal zone V or VE may be written and in the flood zones where an accepted Elevation Certificate must be on file before binding. An accepted certificate must also be recent: its survey date may lie no more than the tier's maximum certificate age before receipt.

| Tier | Excess Flood 250K | Excess Flood 500K | Excess Flood 1M | Excess Flood 2M | Excess Flood 3M | Excess Flood 5M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home in zone V or VE may be written | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Lowest floor height above base flood elevation required on the accepted certificate for a V-zone home, whole feet | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Flood zones in which an accepted Elevation Certificate is required to bind | V, VE | V, VE | V, VE | V, VE | A, AE, AH, AO, V, VE | A, AE, AH, AO, V, VE |
| Oldest survey date accepted, with no alteration since, years before receipt | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 |

## Reading the table

- Excess Flood 250K and Excess Flood 500K exclude zone V and VE homes outright; the elevation row for V-zone homes therefore bears only on the four higher tiers.
- On Excess Flood 1M, 2M, 3M and 5M a V or VE home is written only with an accepted certificate showing the lowest floor at least 1 whole foot above the base flood elevation.
- Excess Flood 3M and 5M extend the certificate requirement to zones A, AE, AH and AO.
